subject: POC traffic hypothesis & ownership — FinServe trial next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Shaw <ellen@finserve.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@finserve.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: POC traffic hypothesis & ownership — FinServe trial next steps

Hi Ellen / Rajiv — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth as we scope the POC. Please confirm or correct anything that doesn’t match your expectations.

Summary (what we heard)
- Goal: 4-week POC to validate latency and cost at peak traffic for FinServe’s document-summarization API. Production target: 99th percentile latency <= 350ms and cost <= $0.0008/token.
- Success criteria (proposal):
  1) End-to-end 99th % latency under 350ms for your 95% traffic windows (see windows below)
  2) No more than 5% failure rate on calls (client/retry errors) during steady-state testing
  3) Qualitative acceptance on summary fidelity (sample set)

Traffic hypothesis (we need confirmation)
- Average sustained RPS: ~18 requests/sec (internal estimate from your diagram)
- Concurrency: ~40 concurrent connections at peak
- Burst profile: short bursts up to 220 RPS for 20–30s during end-of-hour batch jobs
- Typical token lengths: prompt 120–350 tokens; expected response 180–600 tokens (median ~320)
- Session patterns: ~65% single-request sessions, ~35% multi-turn (2–4 requests within 2 minutes)
- Telemetry we require: sample request logs (timestamps, input prompt length, model_id placeholder) and 1 hour of peak traces to reproduce a high-burst window.

Proposed deliverables and owners
- FinServe: provide a 48–72h sample traffic file in CSV format (see attached finserve_traffic_sample.csv) by Tue 2026-09-22 — action: Ellen / Rajiv
- Redwood: produce a baseline runbook and resource plan and a mapping of expected GPU pool needed — action: Olga; due Wed 2026-09-23
- Redwood infra: reserve a canary pool for burst simulation and run initial cost projection — action: Ben; due Thu 2026-09-24
- Validation & fidelity: coordinate a 20-sample summary-eval with FinServe stakeholders during week 1 — action: Markus & Ellen; due Fri 2026-09-25

Operational notes
- We will emulate the bursts with a synthetic driver based on your CSV. We need per-request token lengths and inter-arrival times (or an approximate distribution).
- If you have SLA exceptions or special routing (EU region or sensitive customers), flag them now so we can set up routing and data controls.

Attachments: finserve_traffic_sample.csv (csv, stub 42KB) — example rows and column schema included; poc-success-metrics.md (md, 6KB) — proposed pass/fail criteria template.

Next steps: please reply with the CSV or a timeframe when your infra team can drop it into the shared Drive link (or we can accept a HubSpot attachment). Once we have the CSV we’ll schedule the baseline run and send a canary window that mirrors one of your identified peaks.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187
From: Ellen Shaw <ellen@finserve.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@finserve.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 17:54:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC traffic hypothesis & ownership — FinServe trial next steps

Thanks Olga — that all aligns well with what we discussed. A few clarifications: 
- Sustained RPS should be closer to 22 RPS during market hours (08:00–18:00 ET). Our prior note underestimates peak.
- Bursts: we’ve seen minute-level bursts up to 260 RPS during report generation windows; good to plan for 300 RPS headroom.
- Token lengths: your ranges are right; occasional long responses can go up to 1,200 tokens for large documents but those are <2% of traffic.

We’ll get you a 72h traffic export by Tue 09/22. I’ll send the CSV to the Drive link you provided and drop a HubSpot attachment as backup.

Quick ask: can you confirm the CSV columns you need? We’ll include: timestamp (ms), user_id (hashed), prompt_length, response_length, endpoint_name, status_code.

Appreciate the clear owners — Ellen

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: infra prep & data mapping for FinServe POC

Markus / Olga — internal checklist as I start the infra prep: 
- Can you confirm whether FinServe will include endpoint_name mapping in the CSV? That will let us map to different models/routing rules. Ellen asked above — please confirm.
- I’ll pre-provision a 3-GPU canary pool (A100-class equivalent) and a 6-GPU test pool for the full run. If token lengths spike to ~1,000–1,200 for a small subset, we’ll need to ensure KV cache sizing supports longer sequences.
- Dev Patel will own the synthetic driver script and load-profile generation; I’ll loop him in after we get the CSV.

Tentative timeline:
- 9/22: receive CSV from FinServe
- 9/23: dry-run on sample subset (low cost)
- 9/24: full canary burst simulation
- 9/27–10/01: 1-week steady-state evaluation (if all ok, push to 2-week verification)

I’ll update the Drive runbook with config snippets and the GPU sizing assumptions (memory/kv-cache).

—Ben
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC traffic hypothesis & ownership — FinServe trial next steps

Thanks for the quick confirmation, Ellen — we’ll plan for the higher headroom. A couple operational notes and the proposed canary window: 

Canary plan
- Canary window: Fri 2026-09-24 14:00–14:30 PT to mirror your reported daily peak (we’ll run three 30s 250–300 RPS bursts within that window).
- Synthetic driver needs: the CSV with timestamp (ms), prompt_length, response_length, and endpoint_name is ideal. If user_id is PII-sensitive you can hash it; we’re fine with hashed/opaque ids.
- Baseline reports: we’ll send a pre-run cost estimate and a post-run readout (latency percentiles, failure rates, token breakdown).

Attachments included: poc-success-metrics.md (template for signoff), finserve_traffic_sample.csv (sample rows).

If the 24th is a hard date for you, reply and we’ll lock it. Otherwise we can shift to Mon 09/27 to give your infra team more time.

—
Olga
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@finserve.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ellen Shaw <ellen@finserve.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:43:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC traffic hypothesis & ownership — FinServe trial next steps

Olga — locking in Monday 09/27 for the canary run would be safer for our ops team. Ellen and I confirmed with our SREs; they’ll upload the 72h export to the Drive by EOD Mon (09/21 PST) — apologies for the timing mismatch, we had a prep task slip.

We’ve included a small sample of the long-response cases in a separate file (long_responses_sample.json) in the Drive; those are the 1–2% of requests that exceed 1k tokens — important for cache sizing.

Confirm: we agree to the success criteria and the post-run readout. Please include a cost projection in the pre-run pack so we can present to procurement.

Thanks,
Rajiv

FinServe Ltd
